test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-II Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In the context of the Revolt of 1857, what did the General Service Enlistment Act of 1856 require of sepoys?

options.text: Compulsory overseas service, violating the religious beliefs of some sepoys
Prohibition on wearing religious symbols such as caste marks or beards
Mandatory conversion of sepoys to Christianity before joining service
Restriction on marrying without the permission of British officers

solution:
The correct answer is __**Compulsory overseas service, violating the religious beliefs of some sepoys**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **General Service Enlistment Act of 1856** was a significant cause of discontent among Indian soldiers (sepoys) during British rule.
 
• This Act mandated that Indian sepoys serving in the British East India Company’s army could be sent overseas for military service.
 
• This provision was deeply resented, as traveling overseas violated the religious beliefs of many Hindu sepoys. According to traditional Hindu customs, crossing the sea (referred to as "Kala Pani") was considered a taboo that led to the loss of caste and religious purity.
 
• The Act also disregarded the cultural and religious sentiments of Indian soldiers, leading to a sense of betrayal and alienation among the sepoys towards their British officers.
 
• This imposition of overseas service became one of the major grievances that contributed to the outbreak of the **Revolt of 1857**, also known as the First War of Indian Independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Revolt of 1857**:

 
 
• The Revolt of 1857 was a significant uprising against British colonial rule in India, starting in **Meerut** and spreading to other parts of India.
 
• It was caused by various factors, including political, economic, social, and religious grievances of the Indian people.
 
• The immediate trigger was the introduction of the **Enfield rifle**, which required soldiers to bite off cartridges greased with animal fat, offending both Hindu and Muslim religious beliefs.
 
 
 
• **Impact of General Service Enlistment Act:**
 
 
• The Act undermined the trust and loyalty of Indian soldiers towards the British administration.
 
• It was seen as an intentional move to interfere with the religious practices of Indian sepoys, further fueling discontent.
 
 
 
• **Cultural and Religious Sensitivities:**
 
 
• Hindu soldiers were reluctant to cross the sea because it was believed to result in the loss of their caste and religious purity, a significant concern in the rigid caste-based society of India.
 
• The British administration failed to respect these cultural and religious customs, exacerbating tensions.
 
 
 
• **Other Causes of the Revolt of 1857:**
 
 
• The **annexation of territories** under the Doctrine of Lapse, which denied Indian rulers their right to succession, angered many princely states.
 
• The introduction of **British laws** and the erosion of traditional Indian practices were perceived as an attack on Indian culture and sovereignty.
 
• The economic exploitation of Indian resources and industries, coupled with heavy taxation, caused widespread poverty and discontent among the masses.
 
 
 
• **Important Events of the Revolt:**
 
 
• The revolt began on **10 May 1857** in Meerut, where sepoys rebelled against their British officers.
 
• Prominent leaders of the revolt included **Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi**, **Bahadur Shah II**, **Tantia Tope**, and **Nana Sahib**.
 
• Despite initial successes, the revolt was ultimately crushed by the British in 1858, leading to significant changes in British policies towards India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **General Service Enlistment Act** was one of the many factors that led to the alienation of Indian soldiers and their decision to revolt against British rule.
 
• While the British intended the Act to enhance military flexibility, it ended up being a key factor in the growing unrest among the sepoys, contributing to the larger rebellion.
 
• The Revolt of 1857 marked the **end of the East India Company’s rule** and led to the direct control of India by the British Crown under the **Government of India Act, 1858**.
 
• The events of 1857 are often regarded as the first significant step towards India’s independence from British colonial rule.
